title: gpu-occupancy-nsight-notes-q4-2024
summary: Raw notes and preliminary analysis from a set of Nsight runs focused on GPU occupancy and wall-time hotspots for the 16B transformer generation path. Goal: identify whether kernels are compute-bound, memory-bound, or latency-limited and propose short experiments to improve throughput and tail latency.
content:
Context:
- Target workload: generation path for a 16B transformer variant (seq len 1024 warm, typical inference seq 128) used in Hosted API. Running on AWS p4d (A100 40GB) nodes for these experiments. Batch sizes tested: 1, 4, 8 for streaming token generation.

What I captured:
- Tools: nv-nsight-cu-cli (local headless), Nsight Systems for timeline snapshots, CUDA Graph capture verification via our runtime.
- Metrics pulled: sm__throughput.avg, sm__inst_issued.sum, sm__warps_active.avg, sm__lts_pipe_utilization.avg, sm__sass_thread_inst_executed_per_inst, dram__bytes.sum, l2_read_transactions, achieved_occupancy (from kernel timeline).
- Traces: full kernel timeline (first 3 tokens of a generation), separate long-run capture for steady-state token gen (1000 tokens, low-sampling).

High-level observations:
1) Average SM utilization ~42% during steady-state token generation (batch=4, seq=128). Spikes to ~78% during large GEMM phases (FFN), but attention phases show lower sustained utilization (~30%).
2) Achieved occupancy reported per-key kernels:
   - fused_attention_forward: occupancy ~0.36 (36%), active_warps_per_SM ~22, theoretical max warps 64.
   - cublasLt_gemm (matmul for FFN): occupancy ~0.62 (62%), near compute bounds when cuBLAS fused kernels run.
   - embedding_lookup / token_projection: occupancy ~0.18, heavy memory bound (dram throughput high, warp stall due to memory).
3) Warp execution efficiency: 78% on average; warp stalled reasons: memory (L2->DRAM) dominated in attention key/value scatter and embedding paths.
4) L2 utilization spikes when KV cache is hot; L2 read bandwidth indicates many small scattered reads during KV gather causing serialization.
5) Kernel launch overhead: CPU-side gaps between graph nodes measured ~300-500us for baseline (no CUDA Graphs), reduced to ~20-40us with CUDA Graph capture + launch. This corresponded to ~12% reduction in tail latency for batch=1.

Detailed timeline notes (nsight sys snapshots):
- Timeline shows alternating cublasLt matmuls and custom attention kernels; attention kernels have many short, back-to-back launches (<200us each) leading to high kernel launch overhead.
- Memory copies (device<->host) occur rarely in steady state; most data movement is device-device and within GPU caches.
- Kernel fusion candidate: attention K/V transpose + small matmuls + softmax could be fused into a single kernel to reduce intermediate global memory pressure and kernel launches.

What seems to be limiting perf by phase:
- FFN (dense matmul + bias + activation): compute-bound; cuBLAS kernels near peak for FP16. Occupancy is good.
- Attention (fused_attention_forward): partially memory bound due to scattered KV access and multiple small GEMMs. Low occupancy because kernels launch with small thread-block counts to handle variable sequence lengths and irregular memory access.
- KV cache management: L2 thrashing observed for long sequences where old KV entries get evicted; L2 hit-rate drop correlates with increased DRAM reads and lower SM utilization.

Representative commands used (nsight headless):
- nv-nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all -f --metrics sm__throughput.avg,sm__warps_active.avg,sm__inst_issued.avg,sm__achieved_occupancy.mean,dram__bytes.sum -- ./build/bin/serve_local --profile-run --model 16B --batch 4 --seq 128
- nsys profile --output=trace.nsys --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,cublas --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./build/bin/serve_local --profile-run --tokens 1000
- Small helper: python scripts/parse_nsight_metrics.py --input metrics.csv --metric sm__achieved_occupancy.mean --aggregate mean

Quant numbers (representative):
- Batch=1, seq=128 steady-state token: tail 95p latency before CUDA Graphs 220ms, after 190ms.
- Batch=4, seq=128 throughput (tokens/s) before graph capture: 8600; after: 9200 (+7%).
- fused_attention_forward average occupancy: 36% (expected 48-64%), avg L2 read transactions increase by 2.1x vs cuBLAS heavy sections.
- cublasLt matmul peak SM utilization: 78-85% during runs; GFLOPS ~120 TFLOPS (fp16, theoretical 312 TFLOPS for full chip — note we run mixed precision kernels and some memory-bound phases lower that).

Primary hypotheses derived from traces:
- Hypothesis A: Attention kernels are under-occupying because we intentionally bound blockDims to avoid register spilling for large hidden sizes; this reduces resident warps and hence occupancy. We can re-evaluate register vs occupancy tradeoff by profiling with smaller register footprint (compiler flags) and slightly larger blockDim.
- Hypothesis B: KV scatter/gather causes L2/DRAM pressure; changing layout (AoS -> SoA) for KV representation or blocking the KV gather into coalesced units will improve L2 hit rates and reduce DRAM stalls.
- Hypothesis C: Kernel launch overhead is non-trivial for low-batch/streaming scenarios; enabling CUDA Graph capture for the generation path yields meaningful latency reduction and modest throughput gains.

Short experiments to run next (ordered):
1) Run a variant build allowing higher thread occupancy (compiler pragmas to reduce register usage) for fused_attention_forward and compare achieved_occupancy & warp efficiency. Metric: sm__achieved_occupancy.mean, sm__warp_efficiency.
2) Implement an alternate KV memory layout (blocked SoA) in a branch and run same nsight metrics. Verify L2 read transactions drop and DRAM read bytes decrease.
3) Capture CUDA Graph path end-to-end under realistic interleaving (multiple clients) and measure scheduler behavior; check whether graph reuse covers common token generation patterns.
4) Micro-benchmark attention softmax + scale in fused kernel to check if we can merge softmax into attention matmul output stage.

Risks and caveats:
- Occupancy alone is not definitive — some kernels purposefully trade occupancy for reduced register pressure and fewer memory spills. Need to correlate occupancy changes with GFLOPS and observed latency.
- Nsight headless runs can perturb timing (sampling/collection overhead); ensure multiple runs and warmup windows to avoid cold start skew.
- CUDA Graphs complicate debugging and dynamic branching; must validate correctness across corner cases (variable seq lengths, early stopping).

Notes to devs / next actions:
- @Ethan: can you run the register-reduced build on p4d and collect sm__achieved_occupancy.mean + sm__warp_efficiency for a 1/4/8 batch sweep? Put raw CSVs in the same perf-investigations folder.
- @Lucas: please prototype blocked SoA KV layout in a branch; no need to optimize, just correctness + perf traces.
- @Priya: validate CUDA Graph capture for the generation loop in dockerized private deployment (we need to ensure graph creation works with our allocator hooks).

Appendix: quick checklist when reproducing profiling runs:
- Kill background CUDA processes (nvidia-smi to verify)
- Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to single GPU for deterministic traces
- Warmup with 200 tokens generation before capturing
- Use --profile-run flag to enable deterministic scheduling in runtime

Bottom line: attention path and KV handling are the largest levers. FFN is healthy. CUDA Graphs give easy wins for latency-sensitive single-shot requests. Next week experiments should focus on occupancy vs regs and KV memory layout.

Unresolved questions (for alignment meeting):
- Do we accept a small increase in register spills to improve occupancy for attention kernels? How much complexity does that add to maintenance?
- For private deployment, will customers accept CUDA Graphs (some environments restrict capture)? Need to document fallback path and config toggle.

This doc is intended as a working notes file; I'll convert key findings into a short confluence brief once experiments complete.
findings: Low occupancy on fused_attention_forward (~36%) due to conservative thread/block config and irregular memory access. FFN matmuls are compute-bound and healthy. CUDA Graph capture reduces kernel-launch overhead and improves tail latency notably for batch=1. KV layout causes L2/DRAM pressure and contributes to warp stalls.
recommendations: 1) Run register-usage vs occupancy experiment for attention kernels. 2) Prototype blocked SoA KV layout to improve coalescing. 3) Enable and validate CUDA Graph capture in runtime for generation hot path (config flag). 4) Add nsight metrics to CI perf job for regression monitoring.
